this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context‑
(i) 'employment" means any

sections.shortTitle: West Pakistan Essential Services Maintenance In Force in Sindh Act 1958
sections.description:
Power to order persons engaged in certain employments to remain in specified areas.

SIND ESSENTIAL SERVICES (MAINTENANCE) ACT, 1958
SIND ESSENTIAL SERVICES (MAINTENANCE) ACT, 1958
(Published in the Gaz. of West Pakistan Extr., 25 April 1958, p.
719.)
[25 April, 1958]
West Pakistan Act No. XXXIV of 1958
An Act
to provide for the maintenance of certain
essential services.
4. Power to order persons
engaged in certain employments to remain in specified areas.‑(1) The
Government or an officer authorised in this behalf by the Government may, (Words added by
W. P. Ord. XXXIV of 1965, s. 3 and Sch. II.) [if the public interest so requires,] by general or special
order, direct that any person or persons engaged in any employment or class of
employment to which this Act applies shall not depart out of such area or areas
and for such period not exceeding three months as may be specified in such
order.
(2) An order made under sub‑section
(1) shall be published in such manner as the Government, or the officer making
the order, considers best calculated to bring it to the notice of the persons
affected by the order.

sections.shortTitle: West Pakistan Essential Services Maintenance In Force in Sindh Act 1958
sections.description:
Offences

SIND ESSENTIAL SERVICES (MAINTENANCE) ACT, 1958
SIND ESSENTIAL SERVICES (MAINTENANCE) ACT, 1958
(Published in the Gaz. of West Pakistan Extr., 25 April 1958, p.
719.)
[25 April, 1958]
West Pakistan Act No. XXXIV of 1958
An Act
to provide for the maintenance of certain
essential services.
5. Offences.‑Any
person engaged in any employment or class of employment to which this Act
applies who‑
(a) disobeys any lawful order
given in the course of such employment, or attempts to persuade any person to
disobey any such order , or
(b) without reasonable excuse
abandons such employment of absents himself from work, or
(c) departs from any area
specified in an order under sub‑section (1) of section 4 without the
consent of the Government or the authority making that Order, and any employer of a person engaged in an employment or class of employment to
which this Act applies, who without reasonable excuse‑
(1) discontinues the employment
of such person, or
(2) by closing an establishment
in which such person is engag ed, causes discontinuance of his employment, or
(3) discontinues or causes the
discontinuance of an essential service, is guilty of an offence under this Act.
Explanation 1.‑The
fact that a person apprehends that by continuing in his employment he will be
exposed to increased physical danger is net reasonable excuse within the
meaning of clause (b).
Explanation 2.‑A
person abandons his employment within the mean ing of clause (b) who,
notwithstanding that it is an express or implied term of his contract of
employment that be may terminate his employment on giving notice to his
employer of his intention to do so, so terminates his employment without the
previous consent of his employer.

sections.shortTitle: West Pakistan Essential Services Maintenance In Force in Sindh Act 1958
sections.description:
Regulation of wages and conditions of service

SIND ESSENTIAL SERVICES (MAINTENANCE) ACT, 1958
SIND ESSENTIAL SERVICES (MAINTENANCE) ACT, 1958
(Published in the Gaz. of West Pakistan Extr., 25 April 1958, p.
719.)
[25 April, 1958]
West Pakistan Act No. XXXIV of 1958
An Act
to provide for the maintenance of certain
essential services.
6. Regulation of wages and
conditions of service.‑(1) The Government May make. rules regulating
or empowering specified authorities to regulate the wages and other conditions
of service of persons or of any class of persons engaged in any employment or
class of employment to which this Act applies.
(2) When any such rules have been
made or when any directions regulating wages or conditions of service have been
given by the authority empowered by such rules to give them, any person failing
to comply there with is guilty of an
offence under this Act.

sections.shortTitle: West Pakistan Essential Services Maintenance In Force in Sindh Act 1958
sections.description:
Penalties and procedure

SIND ESSENTIAL SERVICES (MAINTENANCE) ACT, 1958
SIND ESSENTIAL SERVICES (MAINTENANCE) ACT, 1958
(Published in the Gaz. of West Pakistan Extr., 25 April 1958, p.
719.)
[25 April, 1958]
West Pakistan Act No. XXXIV of 1958
An Act
to provide for the maintenance of certain
essential services.
7. Penalties and procedure.‑(1)
Any person found guilty of an offence under this Act, shall be punishable with
imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and shall also be liable
to a fine.
(2) Where the person accused of
an offence under this Act‑is a com pany or other body corporate, every
director, manager, secretary or other officer thereof shall, unless he proves
that the offence was committed with out his knowledge or that he exercised due
diligence to prevent the commis sion of the offence be liable to the punishment
provided for the offence.
(3) No court shall take
cognizance of an offence under this Act except upon complaint in writing made
by an officer empowered by the Government in this behalf.
sections.punishment:
punishable with

sections.shortTitle: West Pakistan Essential Services Maintenance In Force in Sindh Act 1958
sections.description:
Saving of effect of laws imposing liability to national service.

SIND ESSENTIAL SERVICES (MAINTENANCE) ACT, 1958
SIND ESSENTIAL SERVICES (MAINTENANCE) ACT, 1958
(Published in the Gaz. of West Pakistan Extr., 25 April 1958, p.
719.)
[25 April, 1958]
West Pakistan Act No. XXXIV of 1958
An Act
to provide for the maintenance of certain
essential services.
9. Saving of effect of laws
imposing liability to national service. Nothing contained in this Act or
in any declaration or order made there under, shall have effect in derogation
of any provision of law which is or may be for the time being in force,
imposing upon a person engaged in an employment or class of employment to which
this Act applies any liability to be caked up for national service or to
undertake employment in the national service.
